page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM hypervisor technology. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, configured with 8 physical cores supporting hyperthreading for 16 vCPUs. The processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX, AVX-512, and AVX512_VNNI instruction sets. The instance delivers 64 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4 GB of RAM per vCPU core. It has no bundled local storage, relying on attached block storage, and includes a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth limit.

Performance benchmarks indicate a split between single-core and multi-core output. Single-threaded tests show lower throughput, with stress-ng single-core CPU execution and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the bottom 25% relative to comparable instances. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks—including Geekbench multi-core, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded stress-ng—demonstrate performance within the average 50% range. Memory bandwidth performance for uncached read and write blocks remains average. Workload benchmarks record steady output, with Redis SET operations achieving 13.43 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 11.32 GB/sec.

The ecs.g6.4xlarge offers a balanced resource profile suitable for enterprise workloads requiring consistent multi-core execution rather than peak single-threaded speed. The lack of local disk storage means disk IOPS depend entirely on attached cloud storage solutions. Given its 5 Gbps network baseline and balanced memory configuration, this instance provides effective resource density for web application backends, container orchestration nodes, enterprise software compilation, and general-purpose database applications.

The instance lacks local disk storage, relying on external network volumes. Benchmark evaluations show single-core execution speed in the bottom quartile, whereas multi-core compute, memory bandwidth, and synthetic database performance fall within the average range, including 13.43 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.32 GB/sec static web serving throughput. The resource balance makes ecs.g6.4xlarge well suited for general-purpose workloads, web applications, microservices, and software compilation tasks.
